:::{#thm-convex-max}
#### The maximum of convex functions is convex

If $f_1$ and $f_2$ are [convex](algebra.qmd#def-convex-function) functions on $\reals^p$,
then $f(\vx) \eqdef \max\cb{f_1(\vx), f_2(\vx)}$ is convex.

:::

::: proof

Let $\vx, \vy \in \reals^p$ and $t \in [0, 1]$. For $i = 1, 2$,

$$
\ba
f_i(t \vx + (1 - t) \vy)
&\le t f_i(\vx) + (1 - t) f_i(\vy)
&& \text{(} f_i \text{ is convex)}
\\
&\le t f(\vx) + (1 - t) f(\vy).
&& \text{(} f_i \le f \text{, and } t, 1 - t \ge 0 \text{)}
\ea
$$

Both $f_1$ and $f_2$ at $t \vx + (1 - t) \vy$ are at most $t f(\vx) + (1 - t) f(\vy)$,
so their maximum $f(t \vx + (1 - t) \vy)$ is too.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-convex-max}
#### A maximum is convex; a minimum need not be

- $f_1(x) = x$ is convex, by the computation for $2x + 1$ in @exm-strictly-convex with $2$ and $1$ replaced by $1$ and $0$,
  and $f_2(x) = x^2$ is convex by the same example, so $\max\cb{x, x^2}$ is convex by @thm-convex-max.
- The minimum of two convex functions need not be convex:
  $g(x) = \min\cb{x^2, (x - 2)^2}$ has $g(0) = g(2) = 0$,
  but at the midpoint $g(1) = \min\cb{1, 1} = 1 > \tfrac{1}{2} g(0) + \tfrac{1}{2} g(2) = 0$.

:::
